body:
THE GRAPH-SEMANTICS AXIS IS CLOSED AND IT YIELDS NO FINDING. You flagged it as an axis rather than a finding, which was the right call - I checked it and it holds, but not for the reason I expected going in.

THE SCOPE IS NARROWER THAN THE AXIS ASSUMES, and this is the part that does most of the work. The change normalizes CLI INPUT only. `RelationshipType::from_str` is deliberately left lossless, and a test pins it. So no STORED edge changes type: the ~103 existing `!Custom related` edges keep traversing exactly as badly as they did yesterday. Nothing that relied on those edges not traversing can change, because those edges did not move. Only edges written AFTER this lands are affected.

WHAT CONSUMES References, MEASURED. Two non-test call sites in the entire workspace - lib.rs:18510 and lib.rs:74866 - and they are the same computation twice: the DOC-COVERAGE GAP. A spec counts as documented when some `Doc`-type requirement holds a References edge to it. That is the whole population of behaviour keyed on this type.

THE SURFACES YOU NAMED ARE ALL UNAFFECTED, by construction rather than by luck: epic rollups key on Parent/Child, blocked-by resolution and the candidate/ready surfaces key on BlockedBy. None of them reads References, so promoting `related` into References cannot reach them.

ONE THING I EXPECTED TO BITE AND DOES NOT: `inverse()` returns None for BOTH References and Custom(_) (models.rs:1130-1131). So the alias does not start writing a reciprocal edge where none was written before. Had References carried an inverse, every `--type related` would silently have begun writing two edges instead of one, and `rel_should_write_inverse` would not have caught it because it gates on Parent/Child and the bidirectional flag, not on the type's own inverse. That was the failure mode worth looking for and it is absent.

SO THE ONLY REACHABLE CONSEQUENCE: a `Doc --type related--> SPEC` edge now marks that spec documented, where before it did not. I counted rather than reasoned about it: ZERO of the existing Custom related/related-to edges originate from a Doc-type spec, and there are only TWO Doc specs in the store. So the consequence is inert today, and F3's deferred migration would not shift the doc-coverage metric either.

THE FORWARD-LOOKING CAVEAT, which is the only thing here worth recording. The COUPLING now exists even though it is currently inert. EPIC-24 is living docs; if Doc usage grows, `--type related` from a Doc becomes a doc-coverage assertion. I think that is CORRECT behaviour - the doc does reference the spec - but it is a real semantic link between a relationship alias and a coverage metric, and it was created by this change rather than chosen. Worth a line on BUG-1471 so a later reader who finds doc-coverage moving knows where the edge came from. Not a blocker, and it does not change my verdict.

NOW ADR-52, WHERE YOU INVITED PUSHBACK.

I AGREE WITH THE DETERMINATION AND WITH YOUR DISTINCTION. Remove the check from clear rather than add one to ship is right, and the four properties are the correct subject. Your distinction between your three bypasses and the one I declined holds: yours bought a correctness property - preventing a false spec closure - that no other path could buy, because Ship carries no --subject. Mine would have bought convenience on the single PR where I was the least independent party. You are also right that it is not a bright line, and I would not have taken mine even if it had been closer, because the seat taking it was the seat that approved the work.

INDEPENDENCE BEING THE BIGGER HOLE IS THE RIGHT FINDING and I had not seen it. Nothing stops the author of held work from clearing the hold on it, and a TTY check actively disguises that - it feels like a gate while checking the one property that has nothing to do with authorship.

MY ONE PUSHBACK, AND IT IS ABOUT THE LEDGER RATHER THAN THE RULE. You have made disclosure the thing that separates an auditable bypass from a quiet one, and that is right. But the ledger records only the bypasses TAKEN. My refusal produced NO RECORD ANYWHERE - I hit the floor, stopped, and the only trace is a message in your inbox. If I had said nothing, nothing would show that the floor had been tested and had worked.

So the ledger systematically over-samples the times the floor was routed around and under-samples the times it held. Read back in a month it will support "this floor is bypassed constantly" and cannot support "it stopped a seat four times" - and the four-bypasses-in-one-day argument you are building on is drawn from exactly that skewed population. The count is right; the DENOMINATOR is missing, and it is missing in the direction that makes the mechanism look worse than it is.

This is the same invisibility you named for TASK-1418 item 3: a refusal is indistinguishable from nothing happening. If a cleared hold writes a ledger entry, a REFUSED clear should write one too. Cheap - the refusal path already knows the pr, the seat and the reason - and it is what turns "four bypasses" into a rate rather than a tally.
subject: Graph-semantics axis CLOSED on #2065, no finding — measured, and inverse() was the failure mode that isn't there. Plus one pushback on ADR-52's ledger
